body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau=(-\widehat a_T-\nabla\widehat\phi_T(\widetilde y_j))_{j=1}^J,\qquad \sqrt{n/L_n}\{\widehat\tau-\tau(P)\}\Rightarrow N(0,V(P))\), uniformly over the maintained class.

sampling_model.design: Four mutually independent repeated-cross-section samples indexed by \(g\in\{C0,C1,T0,T1\}\).
sampling_model.units: Within cell \(g\), \(X_{g,1},\ldots,X_{g,n_g}\) are independent draws from \(P_g\), with \(n=\min_g n_g\) and \(n_g/n\to\rho_g\).
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment group is untreated at period zero and exposed at period one; the intrinsic torus changes-in-changes lemma identifies the no-treatment treated-post map from invertible production maps and two \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclically monotone graphs.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cell density is bounded between \(c\) and \(C\) on \(\mathbb T^2\), both nested Brenier Jacobians are uniformly elliptic, and the selected population lift branches remain \(\beta\)-separated from lattice boundaries and the squared-distance cut locus.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each of the four independent cell densities is estimated by the declared order-\(s\) signed periodized KDE, clipped at \(c/2\) and renormalized; on the uniform good event clipping is inactive and the normalizer equals one.  A fixed \(a_h\) is chosen in \(1/[2(s-2)],1/6)\), followed by a fixed \(\vartheta>0\) satisfying \(a_h(6+4\vartheta)<1\).  The map and covariance calculations solve the augmented scalar--harmonic systems, use opposite-fold adjoint pilots, retain all generated-target cross products, and add \(n^{-1}I_{2J}\) before block inversion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 29 proves a \(\sqrt{n/\log(1/h_n)}\) pointwise Gaussian limit with covariance \(I_2/(4\pi)\) when source and target are uniform on \(\mathbb T^2\).  The present result recovers that constant in the known-cell reduction and extends the dimension-two phenomenon only on the stronger smooth, positive, uniformly elliptic, selected-no-cut, fixed-grid, independent-four-sample torus class.

Theorem 3.2 differentiates a Brenier map along one smooth target-density curve through a linearized Monge--Ampere problem; the present derivative treats two varying endpoints, nonzero selected torus translations, four inputs, and a generated target.

Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 identify the multivariate changes-in-changes counterfactual on proper convex Euclidean supports under cyclic comonotonicity.  The intrinsic squared-distance flat-torus identification here is a distinct theorem, not an extension of that Euclidean support result.

Section 3, Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 identify a gradient-Green influence and its pole singularity, but do not prove the shrinking-bandwidth four-sample nested empirical central limit theorem established here.
Theorems 2.4 and 2.10 give a weak functional limit and bootstrap for empirical Brenier potentials and fixed weighted contrasts, not pointwise gradients.

Theorems 2 and 6 give near-matching global \(L^2\) minimax rates for one smooth transport map through wavelet semi-dual estimation and a Fano lower bound; the present result instead gives a nested fixed-grid Hellinger-local logarithmic rate.
Theorem 18 gives a \(\log n/n\) global squared-risk upper rate for a two-dimensional smooth-density plug-in map without the fixed-grid nested Hellinger-local lower bound proved here.

Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 validate a smoothed bootstrap uniform band for a one-dimensional quantile-represented transport map; the present confidence sets are bivariate but only on a fixed separated grid.

Theorems 2--4 and Corollary 2 derive efficient root-\(n\) inference for scalar effects and distributional estimands under a distributional bridge in paired panel data; neither their estimand nor their dependent sampling design is claimed here.

body.tldr: Under the intrinsic flat-torus changes-in-changes assumptions, the observed nested Brenier functional is proved to equal the selected-lift no-treatment displacement.  For four independent smooth positive samples and the order-\(s\) positive-normalized periodized KDE, the uniform variable-coefficient Green analysis closes on the maximal polynomial window \(1/[2(s-2)]\leq a_h<1/6\).  It yields the full four-cell covariance, the \(\sqrt{n/L_n}\) fixed-grid Gaussian limit, consistent cross-fitted adjoint covariance, simultaneous multiplier ellipses, and matching \(L_n/n\) squared-risk upper and Hellinger-local lower rates.

project_justification.gap: Published changes-in-changes identification on proper convex Euclidean supports does not establish the intrinsic squared-distance torus result, and published transport limit theory does not supply a four-input, generated-target, pointwise-gradient critical law with moving estimated poles and nonzero harmonic translations.
project_justification.niche: In dimension two the Green gradient has logarithmic energy.  Pulling both inner and generated-target equations into treated-post coordinates reduces the singular nested derivative to one outer Green response to four independent cell noises, while the second elliptic response and the selected-translation scores remain bounded in \(L^2\).
project_justification.fill: The note proves the intrinsic identification, the augmented scalar--harmonic derivative, the uniform transformed-kernel parametrix and mixed \(C^{1,\vartheta}\)-by-\(C^{0,\vartheta}\) remainder, the full generated-target covariance, the joint critical Gaussian law, feasible adjoint inference, and matching rate bounds.  The synchronized bandwidth condition is maximal for this proof and excludes \(a_h=1/6\).

body.related_work: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC proves changes-in-changes identification on proper convex Euclidean supports; the intrinsic squared-geodesic full-support flat-torus identification here is separate and is not presented as an extension of that theorem.  Relative to Proposition 29 of ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT, this note generalizes the dimension-two pointwise phenomenon only on the stronger smooth, positive, uniformly elliptic, selected-no-cut, fixed-grid, independent-four-sample torus class, and its known-cell uniform reduction recovers \(I_2/(4\pi)\).  GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization supplies a one-density-path linearization; the present weighted-Hodge argument handles two varying endpoints, translations, and a generated target.  The 2026 Green-influence and potential-limit results do not themselves give the nested shrinking-bandwidth pointwise-gradient law proved here.  HutterRigollet2021Minimax and ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2024Plugin concern global one-map risk, whereas the present converse is fixed-center Hellinger-local and the upper risk is for the nested fixed-grid plug-in.  PonnopratOkanoImaizumi2024UniformBand concerns a one-dimensional uniform band; the present ellipses are bivariate and simultaneous only over a fixed grid.
body.interpretation: The causal target is the selected-lift no-treatment treated-post displacement, whereas \(P\mapsto\tau(P)\) is an observed-law nested optimal-transport functional.  Lem:torus-cic-identification proves their equality under ass:cic-identification and ass:lift-regularity; outside those structural conditions the functional is not assigned a causal meaning.  At a grid point \(y_j\), the limiting block is \(V_j=w_j\sqrt{\det H(y_j)}H(y_j)/(4\pi f_{T1}(y_j))\), where the two control contributions include their generated-target cross terms before squaring.  Distinct fixed-grid points are asymptotically independent, while harmonic translations affect finite-bandwidth covariance but vanish after logarithmic normalization.  Because the limiting blocks are independent and each standardized block is \(\chi^2_2\), the simultaneous deterministic critical value is \(c_{J,\gamma}=-2\log\{1-(1-\gamma)^{1/J}\}\).
body.technical_internal_limitation: The proofs require a two-dimensional flat torus, \(C^s\) densities with \(s\geq8\), common positive density bounds, uniformly elliptic population transports, a selected lift uniformly separated from lattice boundaries and the squared-distance cut locus, four independent samples with stable size ratios, and a fixed separated evaluation grid.  The maximal synchronized polynomial window is open at \(1/6\); at the endpoint the stochastic--stochastic mixed remainder does not vanish.  The result does not cover nonperiodic domains, cut-locus crossings, dependent panels, growing grids, unsmoothed empirical optimal transport, or data-driven bandwidth selection outside the proved window.
body.honest_scope: The note certifies an observed-law functional and its causal interpretation only under the intrinsic torus changes-in-changes representation, then proves fixed-grid Gaussian inference and an \(L_n/n\) rate match on the stronger smooth positive uniformly elliptic selected-no-cut independent-four-sample class.  It does not claim semiparametric efficiency or an exact minimax constant.  A Card--Krueger bivariate employment reanalysis would additionally require a prespecified periodic encoding of the two outcomes, a defensible repeated-cross-section independence approximation, diagnostics for positivity, branch separation and ellipticity, and numerical PDE and adjoint errors negligible relative to \(\sqrt{L_n/n}\).
